mapping: Relaxed feature-to-chemical assignments; collisions remain separate rows and are never summed or averaged.
upstream: Candidate chemical node IDs are topology seeds only. Their numeric seed values are not MOON measurements.
downstream: The selected sensitivity uses PKN-present Factor 1 hepatocyte TF footprint activities with absolute activity greater than 2. Ar and Esr1 are supplied terminal observations, not independently predicted validation targets.
score_construction: ULM scores are calculated with upstream_input=NULL. Factor 1 lipid loadings are joined afterwards for assignment-level sign concordance.
pkn_policy: Only direct chemical-to-protein and protein-to-protein edges from the directionality-audited STITCH exploratory PKN are used. Reaction and metabolite-to-metabolite edges are excluded.
timing: Cross-sectional signatures; no temporal ordering or direct hepatocyte ligand exposure is inferred.
limitations: A relaxed chemical candidate can resolve unmeasured double-bond position, geometry, stereochemistry, sn position, or acid/base state.
One measured lipid can map to multiple chemicals, and related chemical candidates can share direct regulatory edge fingerprints.
MOON scores are generated from TF activities and PKN topology; copied Factor 1 lipid loadings are post-score annotations rather than independent score evidence.
Measured bulk-liver lipid abundance does not establish hepatocyte ligand exposure, receptor engagement, or temporal ordering.
The selected route is a low-threshold sensitivity: no compact strict score-layer solution remained when either tested cutoff exceeded 0.5.
The directional STITCH v5 source files are historical, and all candidate routes remain exploratory mechanistic hypotheses.
